summary.headline: TBO TEK Q2 FY27: GTV up 16% while adjusted EBITDA rose 27%, but management expects a tough Q3 with Middle East and Europe disruption.
summary.overview: Management reported 16% GTV growth and 27% adjusted EBITDA growth for Q2 FY27, its second consecutive quarter of operating leverage. Middle East grew 10% in constant currency and Europe and APAC grew over 30%, despite conflict and October disruptions in Saudi Arabia and European cities. Management said Q3 will be tough and is aiming only for year-on-year growth in top line and bottom line, with the U.S. elections seen as an inflection point. Classic Vacations (acquired about a year ago) is expected to weigh on reported growth, and a Rs. 8.1 crore fraud loss in the UAE subsidiary was flagged as exceptional.

segments.name: Middle East
segments.commentary: Most impacted market due to conflict; grew 10% in constant currency (about 20% reported), still below prior-year baseline; management believes it is gaining share.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Now the largest source market, growing about 36% and about 36% of total GTV; newer markets such as Germany and Eastern Europe grew triple digits on small bases, while UK and Ireland grew on a much larger base.

segments.name: APAC
segments.commentary: Grew north of 30% in the quarter, per management.

segments.name: Classic Vacations (North America)
segments.commentary: Acquired about one year ago; about 20 sales hires added, with about half under six months tenure. Management expects it to be a drag on reported growth near term; TBO sales into Classic rose to about 8% of Classic GTV from about 5% last quarter.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Monthly transacting buyers grew 1% in the quarter and 4% in H1 across about 24,000 quarterly active agents; management is pushing non-air business, which has higher profitability.

segments.name: Hotels
segments.commentary: Management expects hotel GP margins in Q2 levels to hold if conditions stay stable, but may need to change stance if supply rises and demand falls.

guidance_outlook: Q3 expected to be tough; internal aim is year-on-year growth in both top line and bottom line, with constant-currency growth hoped for and currency benefit additional.
Operating leverage expected to hold over the next two to eight quarters if SG&A growth stays below GP growth; trailing 12-month margin suggested as the better guide given seasonality.
No incremental investment needed for operating leverage; upside in GP expected to flow to bottom line.
Classic Vacations expected to show better results over next two to three quarters, with demonstrable results likely by next summer season (Q2 FY28) if macro clears.
Organic air GP take rate guided to range between 1% and 1.2%.
Classic Vacations beta launch of TBO platform for Classic in late November, followed by gradual rollout over several months.
Market development investments to stay unchanged for the rest of FY27; FY28 budget planning to begin in a few weeks.
Working capital release expected to continue positively through end of calendar year.
capex_capacity: Classic Vacations: sales team expanded by about 20 hires; US sales org previously ran with 10-12 staff covering about 10,000 travel advisors, now being scaled up.
Classic: CRM implemented for back-office processes; TBO supply tech integration into Classic completed; TBO platform for Classic in progress.
Supply organisation integrated: Americas and Europe supply teams for TBO and Classic now under common heads.
Pause on new market development for now; AI and automation investment continues in sales and operations tools.
Post-quarter, insurance claim initiated for the UAE fraud loss; additional oversight and automation of processes planned.
demand_pricing: Demand pressure intensified in October after attacks on Saudi airports hit Saudi inbound and outbound travel, with prior bookings cancelled; rioting in European cities (Paris, Madrid, Barcelona, Italy) raised cancellations.
Management is prioritising market share gains via agent penetration, and focusing on dollar revenue stability and high-value transactions over volume.
Organic air take rate fell to about 2% from about 2.3-2.4%, mainly lower airline incentives and lower refund income; management said more than 50% of the impact was passed to travel agents.
Hotel and air GP margins held; organic gross profit margin held at 5.5-5.6% despite lower take rate due to supplier mix (commission vs net models).
Business mix between API and B2A (smaller agents) remained about 50:50; B2A GP margin slightly higher than API.

Management views AI-driven B2C/OTA entry into agency as a threat but limited, citing credit-line knowledge and channel conflict with suppliers; sees complex, high-value itineraries as the defensible segment.

qa_highlights.question: How is demand holding up given elevated international airfares and geopolitical risk, especially at the premium end?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed pressure that intensified in October due to Saudi airport attacks and European rioting; the company is focusing on share gains and dollar revenue stability.

qa_highlights.question: Will H2 be lower than H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to forecast H2 precisely; internal aim is year-on-year growth in top line and bottom line for Q3, with U.S. elections seen as an inflection point.

qa_highlights.question: Will Classic be a drag on overall growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman-level answer: mathematically yes near term, since Classic is not yet growing near 30%; but Classic GP is about double organic GP per dollar of GTV, and its revenue reflects bookings made about a year earlier for groups.

qa_highlights.question: Classic integration milestones and timing of acceleration?
qa_highlights.answer: Sales team ramp and CRM are largely complete; TBO platform beta for Classic due late November, with gradual rollout over several months; results expected within the next couple of quarters, without a firm number.

qa_highlights.question: Rs. 8 crore fraud: what happened and what are the implications for the FEMA penalty?
qa_highlights.answer: Suspected employee collusion led to unauthorised bookings in a government travel agency account in the UAE subsidiary; police complaints filed in India and UAE, insurance claim initiated. FEMA adjudication order received after quarter-end; company will appeal and has not provided, citing high chances of winning.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the air take rate fall and is there reversal potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower incentives and refund income in H1; management expects GP to remain in a 1-1.2% range, with occasional quarterly dips and ad hoc airline incentives.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the rise in FX loss and the working capital release?
qa_highlights.answer: FX loss reflects hedging premium costs plus losses on unhedged exposure (about 25% unhedged) versus last year's gain; working capital release reflected reversal of Middle East overdues and Brazil timing items, plus new credit lines replacing virtual cards, with positive impact expected through year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q3 Classic GTV seasonally weaker than Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 is the weakest quarter for Classic because it books on check-in basis, so Q3 should be better than Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Hotel GP margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to maintain Q2-like hotel margins if conditions stay the same, but may adjust if supply rises and demand falls.

risks_watch: Q3 FY27 visibility is low: Saudi conflict, European rioting, Israeli election outcome and U.S. midterms; prior bookings can reverse on disruptions.
Classic Vacations integration: booking-to-check-in accounting means lumpy revenue; sales ramp and tech rollout timing unclear, and management gave no quantified synergy target.
Take rate compression in air (about 2% vs 2.3-2.5%) and dependence on airline incentives.
FEMA adjudication order received; appeal pending with no provision booked; worst-case outcome not quantified by management.
Fraud investigation at UAE subsidiary ongoing; agency involvement unknown; insurance recovery uncertain.
AI-driven B2C OTA entry into agency business and AI assistants (e.g., Meta and Instinct) as channel disruption risk; management says no imminent threat.
FX loss and hedging cost volatility (hedging about 75% of open exposure).
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term thesis, Classic and operating leverage, but cautious and evasive on Q3 and H2 outlook, declining to give numbers on currency-adjusted growth, Classic synergies or budget plans.

growth.why: Management aims only for YoY growth in top and bottom line in a tough Q3 (no numeric guide), backed by market share gains, SG&A discipline and gross-profit leverage rather than capacity or firm orders; Classic Vacations drag and Middle East/Europe disruption are headwinds.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Adjusted EBITDA grew 27% vs GTV up 16% with constant-currency SG&A growing high single digits, and management expects operating leverage to hold for 2-8 quarters if SG&A growth stays below GP growth; organic GP margin held at 5.5-5.6% but air take rate fell to about 2% from 2.3-2.4%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Classic Vacations sales team added about 20 hires (half under six months tenure) and TBO platform beta due late November with gradual rollout over several months; no physical capacity or plant capex discussed, and market development investments held flat for rest of FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 GTV grew 16% with Europe and APAC over 30% and Middle East 10% constant currency, but India monthly transacting buyers grew only 1% in the quarter and October disruptions in Saudi and Europe hit bookings; Q3 aim is only YoY growth, with no numeric guide.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed; the brief reports no utilisation figure and no new plant or land plan.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined to forecast H2 precisely and only aims for YoY growth in Q3 on top and bottom line, with October disruptions in Saudi and Europe already hitting bookings.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management called Q3 tough with low visibility from Saudi conflict, European rioting and prior-booking cancellations; the Q3 aim is only YoY growth, and a rise in cancellations could push it below that.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: TBO platform beta for Classic Vacations is due late November, followed by gradual rollout over several months, with demonstrable Classic results targeted by summer season Q2 FY28 if macro clears.

rows.label: Classic Vacations results acceleration
rows.why: Management expects Classic to show better results over the next two to three quarters, with demonstrable results likely by summer Q2 FY28 if macro clears, but gave no firm number and Classic is not yet growing near 30%, so it remains a drag on reported growth near term.

rows.label: FEMA adjudication penalty outcome (UAE fraud)
rows.why: A FEMA adjudication order was received after quarter-end with no provision booked; the company will appeal, and the worst-case outcome is not quantified, while the Rs. 8 crore UAE fraud loss has an insurance claim initiated.

rows.label: Air take rate recovery
rows.why: Organic air take rate fell to about 2% from 2.3-2.4% on lower airline incentives and refunds; management guides air GP to 1-1.2% and expects only occasional quarterly dips, so no clear reversal.

tone.note: Management was confident on operating leverage, Classic's long-term thesis and the Europe/APAC growth, but cautious and evasive on Q3 and H2, declining to quantify currency-adjusted growth, Classic synergies or FY28 budget; analysts pressed on the Q3 outlook, Classic drag, demand at the premium end
